text:
A patient may need a tracheostomy when the upper airway is blocked or at risk of blocking (trauma, tumor, swelling, infection, or bilateral vocal cord paralysis), or when they need prolonged mechanical ventilation. It's also used when they can't clear secretions or protect their airway, as after a stroke or with neuromuscular disease. The team note is wrong: the tube sits below the larynx, so it bypasses the cords and doesn't restore their movement or treat the paralysis.
